text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
----SERBIA
POLITIKA
- Serbian government presents first draft version of privatization law; adoption of law expected in May.

- Post Office says it cut off telecommuncations links for privately-owned BK-TV because BK-TV owes it 20 million dinars ($4 million); BK-TV claims it has no outstanding debt and closure is politically motivated.
- Authorities, opposition one step nearer to dialogue on media liberalization.
- Bosnian Serbs continue war crimes trial against Bosnian leader Alija Izetbegovic.
NASA BORBA
- Montenegro' ruling party in nine-hour long debate on prime minister Milo Djukanovic; Djukanovic has support of minority, but manages to hang on to party position.
- Post office restores BK-TV's communications links, TV signal back on air in southern Serbia.
- Education minister says teachers' wages should be further increased.
- Serbian authorities deny BK-TV's claim that they are trying to suppress the station.
- Trade unions say Yugoslav authorities must prepare comprehensive reforms in view of rapidly worsening social situation.
- Montenegrin human rights committee says "libel" sentences pronounced against opposition leaders totally politically motivated.
- Yugoslav Minister for Telecommunications says new law will restore full federal control of all radio and TV frequencies.
- Serbian business tycoon Bogoljub Karic seeks support for candidacy in presidential race.
- Serbia Republic Day, March 28, will be public holiday this year.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Pro-government daily BORBA out to take control of VECERNJE NOVOSTI.
- Yugoslavia, Croatia harmonizing views on dual citizenship laws.
BLIC

- Opinion poll shows Belgrade ex-mayor Nebojsa Covic and ultra-nationalist Vojislav Seselj lead in popularity as prospective presidential candidates in Serbia. President Milosevic expected to assume federal presidency.
----MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Chamber of Commerce and Yugoslav Business Centre in Duesseldorf formed International Business Centre to assist local and foreign companies.
- Radoje Dakic construction machinery plant will not be able to complete planned annual production of 112 machines due to financial problems.
- Niksic bauxite mines plan 68-per cent production increase in 1997.

- Opposition People's Party leader Novak Kilibarda sues Montenegrin leadership for mental aggravation caused by attacks against him in election campaign. Kilibarda hopes membership of his party will support his views at coming emergency congress. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
